info.title: Flow Timers
info.description: Configuration data for the business-timer store (flow-business-timers): named working calendars whose non-working dates are COMPUTED from rules so they never expire, and escalation ladders whose rungs are editable data rather than a compiled-in constant (ADR-001, ADR-031). Materialised by the SeedFlowTimerRegister repair step; OpenRegister does not self-import its own register JSON at boot (ADR-037).

x-openregister.description: Working calendars and escalation ladders for the durable business-timer store. Nothing here sends: a ladder rung names roles, a priority and a message identity that the notification subsystem resolves.

flow-timers.title: Flow Timers
flow-timers.description: Working calendars and escalation ladders consumed by the business-timer store. The timers themselves live in openregister_flow_timers, not here.

working-calendar.title: Working calendar
working-calendar.summary: Which weekdays work, which hours of the day they are open, and which dates are closed.
working-calendar.description: A named working calendar resolved by the business-timer store in the order: the calendar named on the timer, the calendar configured for the subject's organisation, the seeded national default. Non-working dates are computed from rules of kind fixed, easter or observedShift, so the calendar does not expire; enumerated exceptions may accompany rules but a calendar consisting only of enumerated dates is refused. A calendar with no rules at all keeps no holidays, which is an answer rather than an omission: an organisation that works every weekday of the year says so this way. hoursPerWorkingDay is required because without it hours and businessDays are not commensurable, and it is derived from serviceHours when those are declared.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: The calendar's stable name, referenced by a timer's calendar_slug.

organisation.title: Organisation
organisation.description: UUID of the organisation this calendar is configured for. Empty for a shared calendar. The resolution order picks an organisation's calendar when the timer names none.

workingWeekdays.title: Working weekdays
workingWeekdays.description: ISO weekdays (1 = Monday, 7 = Sunday) that are working days.

hoursPerWorkingDay.title: Hours per working day
hoursPerWorkingDay.description: Working hours in one working day. Makes hours and businessDays commensurable.

dayStartsAt.title: Day starts at
dayStartsAt.description: When the working day opens, HH:MM in 24-hour form. It closes hoursPerWorkingDay later, so the two can never disagree. Only elapsed working time reads it; a deadline in business days does not care what time the office opens. Defaults to 09:00.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.description: The zone the organisation counts its days in, as an IANA name such as Europe/Amsterdam. A calendar date becomes a moment only once somebody says where midnight is, and it is the organisation's zone rather than the viewer's: a display preference must not move a statutory deadline. Defaults to UTC.

serviceHours.title: Service hours
serviceHours.description: The hours of the day this calendar's clock runs, per weekday, in the calendar's own zone. One or more windows per weekday, each {start, end} as HH:MM, so a counter that closes over lunch counts the break as closed. A term in hours advances only inside these windows. The shipped calendars declare none on purpose: declaring them moves every deadline in hours on that calendar, and no instance should have its running deadlines recomputed by an upgrade. A Dutch office adds 09:00 to 17:00 on each working day, which is what the admin form offers. A window that ends at or before it starts, two windows that overlap on one weekday, and a window on a day the calendar does not work are refused when the calendar is saved, naming the weekday. When windows are declared, hoursPerWorkingDay is derived from the longest open day, because a calendar with two answers to how long a day is has none.

rules.title: Non-working-date rules
rules.description: Computed non-working-date rules. kind fixed: {month, day, name, observedShift?: {whenWeekday, days}}. kind easter: {offset, name}, offset in days from Easter Sunday. kind observedShift: a fixed date with a required shift. Leave the list empty and the calendar keeps no holidays; it is not required, because refusing a calendar without one told an administrator to invent holidays they do not have.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: fixed: a month/day; easter: an offset in days from Easter Sunday; observedShift: a month/day with a required observed shift.

month.title: Month
month.description: Month of a fixed or observedShift rule; ignored by an easter rule.

day.title: Day
day.description: Day of a fixed or observedShift rule; ignored by an easter rule.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Days from Easter Sunday for an easter rule; ignored by the other kinds.

observedShift.title: Observed shift
observedShift.description: Optional on a fixed rule, required on observedShift: {whenWeekday: weekday name or ISO 1..7, days: integer}.

whenWeekday.title: When weekday
whenWeekday.description: The weekday (name) on which the date shifts, e.g. sunday for Koningsdag.

days.title: Days
days.description: How many days the observed date shifts, e.g. -1 for the Saturday before.

exceptions.title: Exception dates
exceptions.description: Enumerated one-off closures as {date, name}. Allowed alongside rules; refused as the whole calendar.

escalation-ladder.title: Escalation ladder
escalation-ladder.summary: An ordered set of rungs, each a distance from the deadline with the roles, priority and message identity to raise.
escalation-ladder.description: Editable escalation data for the business-timer store. Each rung fires at most once per timer, decided by the unique fire ledger. The rung's roles are resolved against the subject's performer (handler = the assignee) or through roleBindings; the message value is an identity the notification subsystem resolves. Nothing here renders or sends.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: The ladder's stable name, referenced by a timer's ladder_slug.

organisation.title: Organisation
organisation.description: UUID of the organisation this ladder is the default for. Empty for the shared default.

rungs.title: Rungs
rungs.description: Ordered rungs: {key, trigger (preBreach|slaBreached), offset, offsetUnit (hours|businessDays|calendarDays), notifyRole[], escalateToRole[], priority, message, openIncident}.

key.title: Key
key.description: Stable rung identity, e.g. preBreach:14:calendarDays; derived from trigger, offset and unit when absent.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: preBreach fires before the deadline, slaBreached at or after it.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Distance from the deadline, in the offset unit.

offsetUnit.title: Offset unit
offsetUnit.description: The unit of the offset: the same set the SLA accepts.

notifyRole.title: Notify roles
notifyRole.description: Roles told at this rung; handler is the subject's own performer.

escalateToRole.title: Escalate to roles
escalateToRole.description: Roles the matter is escalated to at this rung.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: The urgency the raised transition carries.

message.title: Message
message.description: A message identity the notification subsystem resolves.

openIncident.title: Open incident
openIncident.description: Whether reaching this rung opens an incident.

roleBindings.title: Role bindings
roleBindings.description: Optional map from a role name to a concrete recipient descriptor, e.g. {"teamleader": "group:teamleaders"}. Roles without a binding travel unresolved as role:<name>.
